aspects.fertilizer:
Schemes and App:
Fertilizers are supplied mid-April to mid-September. Input loans run May to October. Punjab extension destroys pre-May 20 nurseries in April-May. Registered farmers receive subsidized seed, weedicides, and zinc sulfate. Khad Hisab mobile app calculates NPK needs.

Nursery:
For weak nursery, broadcast 250 g urea or 400 to 500 g CAN per marla 10 days pre-transplant. For machine trays, apply 1 to 1.5 kg urea per 100 trays 7 to 10 days post-sowing. For nursery zinc deficiency, broadcast 200 g 33%, 250 g 27%, or 300 g 21% zinc sulfate per marla at 2 weeks.

Bag Nutrients (50 kg):
Urea: 46% N (23 kg). CAN: 26% N (13 kg). TSP: 46% P (23 kg). SSP: 18% P (9 kg). DAP: 18% N (9 kg), 46% P (23 kg). Nitrophos: 22% N, 20% P. SOP: 50% K (25 kg). MOP: 60% K (30 kg).

Field Rates:
Limit Al-Khalid to 1 bag urea.
Coarse: 69 kg N, 40 kg P, 25 kg K per acre (planting: 1.75 bags DAP, 0.25 bag urea, 1 bag SOP; then two 1-bag urea splits). Average fertility total: 1.75 bags DAP, 2.5 bags urea, 1 bag SOP.
Basmati fine: 55 kg N, 35 kg P, 25 kg K per acre (planting: 1.5 bags DAP, 0.25 bag urea, 1 bag SOP; then two 0.75-bag urea splits). Average fertility total: 1.5 bags DAP, 1.75 bags urea, 1 bag SOP.
Hybrid coarse: 81 kg N, 46 kg P, 25 kg K per acre (planting: 2 bags DAP, 0.75 bag urea, 1 bag SOP; then two 1-bag urea splits).
Hybrid fine: 69 kg N, 40 kg P, 25 kg K per acre (planting: 1.75 bags DAP, 0.75 bag urea, 1 bag SOP; then two 0.75-bag urea splits).

Timing and Application:
Apply full P, K, and 0.25 bag urea under the last planking. Split remaining N equally twice within 30 to 35 days post-transplant. Or apply P within 6 to 7 days post-transplant, and K half at transplanting and half within 30 days. For Basmati, split N 3 to 4 times every 7 to 10 days, completing before August 20 for late crops. In direct-seeded rice, apply DAP and SOP at sowing, 0.75 bag urea at 30 to 35 days, 0.5 to 0.75 bag as needed, and remainder at 55 to 60 days. Broadcast without standing water.

Soil Adjustments and Green Manure:
Kallar soils require 25% extra N. High-sodium water requires 5 bags gypsum per acre. Apply gypsum on light bara soils. Waterlogged Basmati needs less N. Spray K for severe tubewell K deficiency. For black salt, apply sulfuric acid and gypsum.
Broadcast 15 to 20 kg soaked Jantar seed per acre after wheat, or 8 kg in standing wheat plus 8 kg post-harvest. Rotavate 15 to 20 days pre-transplant with 0.5 bag urea.

Micronutrients and Plant Health:
Apply 6 kg 33%, 7.5 kg 27%, or 10 kg 21% zinc sulfate per acre 10 to 15 days post-transplant or 30 to 35 days post-sowing. Apply 3 kg boric acid 17% or 4.5 kg borax 10.5% at land preparation if omitted previously. Potash suppresses bacterial leaf blight, sheath blight, and brown spot. Excess N worsens leaf folder, planthopper, and blast.
aspects.harvesting:
**Punjab Yield:**
Divide paddy yield by 0.6 to get rice yield; 22.48 maunds per acre yields 37.47 maunds. Punjab averaged 37.47 maunds per acre this year.

**Green Manuring:**
Straw feeds cattle, husk feeds livestock, and flour feeds humans. Post-wheat, plow once, irrigate, and broadcast 15 to 20 kg per acre soaked Jantar seed. Rotavate at flowering 15 to 20 days before Basmati transplanting, hold water, and add half bag urea per acre for rotting.

**Field Irrigation:**
Keep water 1 to 1.5 inches at transplanting, increasing after one week to 2 inches; over 3 inches lowers tillering. In water shortages, 20 to 25 days post-transplanting, hold water 15 days, then aerate 5 to 6 days uncracked. After 50 to 55 days, apply vattar water. Keep wet vattar from booting to grain filling against bhabka, avoiding stagnant water to stop stem rot. Granular poisons require 1.5 to 2 inches standing water for 5 to 6 days. Stop water two weeks pre-harvest.

**Direct Seeded Rice:**
First vattar irrigation occurs after 4 to 5 days. Keep wet vattar 30 days post-germination. Then keep soil moist without standing water, except 3 to 4 days for granular poison. Prevent drought during grain formation. Stop water 15 to 20 days pre-harvest.

**Crop Protection:**
Scout pests every 7 to 10 days in August and September. Spray recommended poisons at economic thresholds, observing pre-harvest intervals. Bacterial leaf blight appears at booting as white damp stripes on leaf tips and edges, drying leaves upward and cutting yield. Destroy diseased debris, remove floating spores during puddle preparation, and rotate crops.

**Harvesting and Machinery:**
Harvest mid-October to 20 November. Hand harvest at 20 to 22 percent moisture when top grains ripen and lower 2 to 3 are filled green. Combine harvest at 100 percent ripeness; avoid harvesting below 18 percent moisture. Use a rice combine or wheat combine with rice attachment. Adjust speeds, slow for lodged crops, check broken or dehusked grains, inspect rear cloth for straw loss, and clean between varieties. Cut higher for super seeders. Machinery: laser leveler, water-tight rotavator, transplanter, DSR drill, combine, straw chopper, super seeder.

**Crop Residues:**
Residue burning destroys organic matter, causes smog, and brings fines and FIRs. Chop and incorporate stubble using a rice straw chopper. Destroy stubble by 28 February.

**Grain Storage:**
Sun-dry grain 4 to 6 days or use dryers to reach 12 to 13 percent moisture, preventing mold and liver cancer-causing aflatoxin. Avoid heaps, jute, and old PP bags. Seal godowns in rain. One week pre-storage, spray walls and floors with deltamethrin or alpha-cypermethrin; never spray grain. Fumigate sealed stores with 25 to 30 aluminum phosphide tablets per 1000 cubic feet for two weeks under expert supervision. Control khapra beetle, snout weevils, and rats using traps, zinc phosphide, or blood-thinning baits.
aspects.irrigation:
Nursery Irrigation:
Broadcast sprouted seed into 1 to 1.5 inches standing water in evening, drain next evening, and add fresh water next morning for 3 to 4 days. Increase depth as seedlings grow, up to 3 inches. Nursery matures in 25 to 30 days. Irrigate 1 to 2 days before uprooting. Discard blight, bakanae, or caterpillar damaged seedlings. Drain transplanter trays 12 hours before planting.

Transplanted Rice Irrigation:
Stand water 5 days, or 3 days during shortage, puddle, and transplant next day. For machine transplanting, puddle 2 days prior, keep water under 1 inch, space rows 12 inches, plants 6 inches, and depth under 2 inches. For manual planting, space hills 9 by 9 inches with 2 plants per hill, giving 80,000 hills and 160,000 plants per acre. Transplant into 1 to 1.5 inches water. Fill gaps within 10 days. Keep 1 to 1.5 inches water for first 7 to 10 days, then increase to 2 inches, never exceeding 3 inches. If water is scarce 20 to 25 days post-transplanting, stand water for 15 days. Aerate field every 5 to 6 days thereafter, keeping soil wet without cracking. Switch to watar irrigations 50 to 55 days post-transplanting. Keep 1.5 to 2 inches water for 5 to 6 days during granular insecticide application. Stop irrigation 2 weeks before harvest.

Direct Seeded Rice Irrigation:
Apply double rouni in first half of May. Drill at 9-inch row spacing and maximum 1.5-inch depth, or broadcast after 1-inch plowing. Apply light irrigation after dry sowing without ponding until emergence. In watar sowing, irrigate after 4 to 5 days. Maintain tar-watar for 30 days post-emergence, then keep soil moist without ponding. Pond water 3 to 4 days for granular pesticides. Prevent drought during grain formation. Irrigate 24 to 36 hours after herbicide sprays. Spray Binaifop 10 EC at 500 ml plus Traibanionser at 800 ml per acre at 3 to 4 weed leaves 12 to 15 days after planting, irrigate 1 day later, pond water 5 days, with 90-day pre-harvest interval. Stop irrigation 15 to 20 days before harvest.

Problem Soils and Disease Management:
In kallar soils, plow deep without puddling, stand water 7 to 10 days before transplanting 35 to 40 day old seedlings, and add 25 percent extra nitrogen. Do not plow deeply in seem thoor soils. Apply 5 bags gypsum per acre with poor quality high-sodium water. Reduce nitrogen on Basmati with seem or coupler. Spray potash for severe deficiency in tubewell-irrigated soils. Keep non-standing water soils tar-watar from booting to grain filling to prevent blast on Super Basmati and Shaheen Basmati. Continuous standing water causes stem rot. Isolate water from fields with stem rot or bacterial leaf blight. Dry field immediately during planthopper attacks.
aspects.machinery:
Land Preparation:
Level fields with a laser land leveler. A water-tight rotavator has extra seals protecting bearings and parts from water, preparing puddling better than traditional plows and planks without machine damage. Puddle fields two days before transplanting for uniform soil in water.

Green Manure:
Broadcast 8 kg per acre Janter seed at the last wheat irrigation. After wheat harvest, irrigate and broadcast another 8 kg per acre. Incorporate Janter into the soil using a disc or rotavator 15 to 20 days before rice transplanting. Apply half a bag of urea for decomposition, deducting this from the next crop fertilizer.

Direct Seeded Rice:
Drill seed into dry soil at 9-inch row spacing and maximum 1.5-inch depth. Inspect pipes regularly to prevent blockages, lift the drill every fourth wheel pass to check seed drop, and fill gaps manually. Apply phosphorus and potash using the drill. Form small borders and apply light irrigation without standing water until emergence.

Nursery Preparation:
Raise seedlings on plastic trays or sheets. One acre requires 100 to 120 trays and 8 to 10 kg certified fungicide-treated seed. Use fertile silt or loam sieved through a 5 mm mesh. If seedlings are weak, broadcast 1 to 1.5 kg urea per 100 trays 7 to 10 days after sowing. Seedlings mature in 25 to 30 days. Drain water from trays 12 hours before transplanting.

Transplanter Operation:
Transplant into uniform standing water under 1 inch deep. Service, grease, and check engine oil before operation. Maintain 12-inch row spacing, 6-inch plant spacing, and planting depth within 1.5 to 2 inches. Disengage planting arms when turning to prevent machine damage, and manually replant missing hills.

Spraying Machinery:
Ensure sprayers do not leak. Use hollow-cone nozzles for insecticides and T-jet nozzles for herbicides. Spray in the morning after dew dries or in the evening, avoiding strong winds. Wear protective gear, masks, and boots. Bury empty pesticide bottles deep in soil.

Combine Harvesting:
Use a rice combine harvester or a wheat combine fitted with a rice attachment. Adjust gear, threshing drum, and blower speed according to the manual. Reduce speed for lodged crops. Do not harvest mechanically if grain moisture drops below 18 percent. Check behind the machine with a cloth for grain loss in straw, and monitor grain cracking. Clean the machine before switching varieties. Cut stubble higher if following with a super seeder.

Residue Management:
Burning crop residue is illegal, causing smog, fines, and FIRs. Use a rice straw chopper to chop stubble into soil. In rice-wheat areas, use zero tillage for timely wheat planting in late October.
aspects.other:
Government and Financial Planning:
Fertilizer supply arrangements take place from mid-April to mid-September.
The Federal Government and the private sector are responsible for fertilizer supply.
Loans for agricultural inputs, fertilizers, and agricultural medicines operate from May to October.
Zarai Taraqiati Bank, commercial banks, and cooperatives are responsible for issuing these loans.

Punjab:
Rice nurseries sown before May 20 are destroyed during April and May.
The Punjab Agriculture Extension Department is responsible for destroying early nurseries.
Remaining stubble from the previous rice crop must be destroyed before or by February 28.
The Punjab Agriculture Extension Department is responsible for stubble destruction.
Modern recommendations on rice cultivation and plant protection are publicized in May using radio, television, newspapers, and loudspeakers.
The Directorate General of Agriculture Extension Punjab, the Directorate of Agricultural Information, and local media are responsible for this publicity.
The Punjab Agriculture Extension Department motivates farmers to cultivate rice at the time of rice sowing.

Harvest and Storage:
Thoroughly dry rice grains before storing them.
Maintain grain moisture content at 12 to 13 percent.
This moisture level prevents aflatoxin problems.

Heat Stress and Varietal Selection:
Severe heat creates difficulties during panicle emergence and affects rice grains.
Severe heat causes pollen death in local varieties, leaving many grains empty.
Select rice seed suited to the specific area.
Cultivate recommended seed varieties to protect the crop from climatic variations.
aspects.overview:
**General Overview:**
Rice is a Kharif crop requiring high water. It meets domestic dietary needs and earns foreign exchange. Rice grown in traditional areas of Punjab is globally renowned for aroma and taste.

**Punjab Government Support:**
A national project to enhance per-acre rice yield under the Prime Minister Agriculture Emergency Program with the Punjab Government has operated in selected Punjab districts since 2019-20. Registered growers receive subsidized certified seeds, weedicides, and zinc sulphate. The program conducts demonstration plots, seminars, farmer days, and yield awareness campaigns.

**Soil and Field Management:**
Clay soil is ideal for rice. It can be cultivated in all soils except sandy soil, including saline and kallar soils with proper care. Apply the recommended fertilizer under the final planking during puddling and transplant nursery seedlings the next day. Adopt mechanical methods for nursery raising and transplanting when facing labor shortages. Direct seeding requires prior training in cultivation methods and weed eradication. Follow certified departmental guidance and manage plant protection against climate change.

**Varieties and Early Sowing:**
Sona Super Basmati matures in 110 to 115 days. Early-sown rice yield in 2024-25 was poor due to weather conditions. The agriculture department has no recommendations for early sowing, so farmers must consult local agricultural experts before planning it.

**Punjab Cultivated Area:**
In 2020-21, Basmati covered 1871.64 thousand hectares (4625 thousand acres), non-Basmati 522.84 thousand hectares (1292 thousand acres), total 2394.48 thousand hectares (5917 thousand acres).
In 2021-22, Basmati covered 1771.68 thousand hectares (4378 thousand acres), non-Basmati 783.46 thousand hectares (1936 thousand acres), total 2555.14 thousand hectares (6314 thousand acres).
In 2022-23, Basmati covered 1678.61 thousand hectares (4148 thousand acres), non-Basmati 510.70 thousand hectares (1262 thousand acres), total 2189.31 thousand hectares (5410 thousand acres).
In 2023-24, Basmati covered 2114.85 thousand hectares (5226 thousand acres), non-Basmati 488.85 thousand hectares (1208 thousand acres), total 2603.70 thousand hectares (6434 thousand acres).
In 2024-25, Basmati covered 2029.09 thousand hectares (5014 thousand acres), non-Basmati 685.13 thousand hectares (1693 thousand acres), total 2714.23 thousand hectares (6707 thousand acres).

**Punjab Rice Production:**
In 2020-21, production in thousand metric tons was 4014.18 Basmati, 1287.20 non-Basmati, total 5301.40.
In 2021-22, production was 3650.00 Basmati, 2129.00 non-Basmati, total 5779.00.
In 2022-23, production was 3731.00 Basmati, 1339.00 non-Basmati, total 5070.00.
In 2023-24, production was 4736.00 Basmati, 1381.00 non-Basmati, total 6117.00.
In 2024-25, production was 4296.00 Basmati, 1734.00 non-Basmati, total 6030.00.

**Punjab Average Yield:**
In 2020-21, Basmati yielded 2146 kg/ha (21.71 of 40-kg units/acre), non-Basmati 2462 kg/ha (24.91 of 40-kg units/acre), total 2214 kg/ha (22.40 maunds/acre).
In 2021-22, Basmati yielded 2060 kg/ha (20.84 of 40-kg units/acre), non-Basmati 2704 kg/ha (27.36 of 40-kg units/acre), total 2257 kg/ha (22.83 maunds/acre).
In 2022-23, Basmati yielded 2060 kg/ha (20.84 of 40-kg units/acre), non-Basmati 2717 kg/ha (27.49 of 40-kg units/acre), total 2262 kg/ha (22.88 maunds/acre).
In 2023-24, Basmati yielded 2240 kg/ha (22.66 of 40-kg units/acre), non-Basmati 2825 kg/ha (28.58 of 40-kg units/acre), total 2349 kg/ha (23.77 maunds/acre).
In 2024-25, Basmati yielded 2117 kg/ha (21.42 of 40-kg units/acre), non-Basmati 2531 kg/ha (25.61 of 40-kg units/acre), total 2222 kg/ha (22.48 maunds/acre).
aspects.pests_diseases:
Punjab Schedule:
Punjab Agriculture Extension releases the production plan by the second week of April. Punjab Seed Corporation distributes rice seed in May and June. DG Pest Warning manages pest scouting and plant protection from the first week of May to the second week of October. 

General Crop Management:
Keep 160000 plants per acre with 80000 holes spaced 9 inches apart and 2 plants per hole. Deeply bury empty pesticide bottles. Spray during mornings or evenings wearing full clothing, mask, and glasses. Use hollow-cone nozzles for insecticides and T-jet nozzles for herbicides. Do not hoe immediately after spraying. Maintain 1.5 to 2 inches of water for 5 to 6 days when applying granular insecticides. Stop watering 2 weeks before harvest.

Nutrient Management:
Change standing water within 10 days of transplanting to manage white kallar. Apply sulfuric acid and gypsum based on soil tests for black kallar. For nursery zinc deficiency, apply 200 grams of 33 percent, 250 grams of 21 percent, or 300 grams of 27 percent zinc sulphate per marla after 2 weeks. In fields, broadcast 6 kg of 33 percent, 7.5 kg of 27 percent, or 10 kg of 21 percent zinc sulphate per acre 10 to 15 days after transplanting. For boron deficiency, apply 3 kg of boric acid 17 percent or 4.5 kg of borax 10.5 percent per acre during land preparation.

Pest Scouting and Thresholds:
Sow nurseries after May 20. Plow rice stubbles by late February to kill stem borer larvae. Stem borer threshold is 4 to 5 moths or 0.5 percent deadhearts in nursery, and 8 to 10 moths or 5 percent deadhearts in fields. Toka threshold is 2 insects per net in nursery, and 3 adults per net or 3 percent damage from May to October. Planthopper threshold is 15 to 20 insects per plant in August-September, and 20 to 25 in September-October. Leaf folder threshold is 2 folded leaves per plant. Black beetle threshold is 1 insect per plant in September-October. 

Diseases and Resistant Varieties:
Super Basmati, Shaheen Basmati, KS-282, KSK-133, IRRI-6, and NIAB IRRI-9 resist blast and bakanae. Always treat seeds with fungicides. For stem rot, avoid continuous standing water 50 to 55 days after transplanting.

Chemical Controls and Pre-Harvest Intervals:
For toka, use bifenthrin 10 percent EC at 250 ml per acre with 30 days interval.
For stem borers, apply cartap 4 percent G at 9 kg or 8 percent G at 4.5 kg with 40 days interval, monomehypo 5 percent G at 7 kg with 14 days interval, or flubendiamide 48 percent SC at 75 ml with 7 days interval.
For leaf folder, apply gamma-cyhalothrin 60 CS at 75 ml with 21 days interval, or emamectin benzoate plus indoxacarb 9 percent SC at 60 to 120 ml with 28 days interval.
For both borers and leaf folder, apply emamectin plus lambda 12 percent WP at 100 ml with 16 days interval, thiocyclam 18.1 percent at 40 to 120 ml with 29 days interval, or tetraniliprole 200 SC at 100 ml with 33 days interval.
For planthoppers, use pymetrozine 50 percent WG at 24 to 30 grams with 14 days interval, sulfoxaflor 240 SC at 80 ml with 7 days interval, or flonicamid 50 percent WG at 60 grams with 7 days interval.
For blast and sheath blight, spray azoxystrobin plus difenoconazole 30 percent SC at 200 ml with 7 to 28 days interval, difenoconazole 250 EC at 125 ml with 14 days interval, or sulfur 80 percent WG at 800 grams with 7 days interval.
For bacterial leaf blight, apply copper hydroxide 77 WP at 200 grams or copper oxychloride 50 percent WP at 250 grams with 14 days interval.
aspects.sowing:
Sowing Dates:
Coarse varieties IRRI-6, KS-282, KSK-133, NIAB IRRI-9, NIAB-2013, KSK-434, Niji-5, NIAB C-195, and KSK-706 sow 20 May to 7 June, transplant 20 June to 7 July. Fine varieties Niji GSR-6, GSR-7, GSR-8, and SKB-32-5-370 sow 10 to 25 June, transplant 10 to 25 July. Al-Khalid sows 25 May to 10 June, transplants 20 June to 10 July. Basmati varieties Vital Super, Sona Super, NIAB S-9, HGT-18, HT-39, Guard-101, PK 2021, NIAB Super, NPR-2, Niji 2020, Super Gold, Super 2019, Basmati 515, Basmati Super, Chenab, Punjab, PK 1121, NIAB 2016, Noor, PK-386, and Sultan Super sow 7 to 25 June, transplant 7 to 25 July. Shaheen Basmati sows 15 to 30 June, transplants 15 to 31 July. Basmati Hybrid KSK-111 sows 7 to 25 June, transplants 2 to 25 July. Coarse hybrids sow 20 May to 15 June, transplant 15 June to 15 July. General Basmati sows 10 to 30 June, transplants 5 to 25 July, preferably early July. Never sow rice before 20 May.

Nursery Methods:
Kaddu method broadcasts sprouted seed into 1 to 1.5 inches standing water, drained nightly for 3 to 4 days, maturing in 25 to 30 days. Per marla seed rate is 1 kg for coarse and 500 to 750 grams for fine varieties. Dry method on loam covers seed with 1 inch straw or husk, maturing in 35 to 40 days. Per marla seed rate is 1.5 kg for coarse and 750 to 1000 grams for fine varieties. Spray weedicide 15 days post-emergence.

Dera Ghazi Khan and Muzaffargarh:
Rab method on hard soils burns 2 inches of dung or straw, mixes ash, and broadcasts dry seed, maturing in 35 to 40 days. Per marla seed rate is 2 kg for coarse and 1 to 1.5 kg for fine varieties.

Transplanting:
Nursery age is 25 to 30 days for kaddu, up to 30 days for Kissan Basmati, and 35 to 40 days for dry or rab methods. Space seedlings 9 inches apart with 2 plants per hole, giving 80,000 holes and 160,000 plants per acre. Keep water depth at 1 to 1.5 inches initially, then 2 inches. Fill gaps within 10 days.

Saline and Waterlogged Soils:
Do not deep plow waterlogged soils. Deep plow saline soils without puddling, and flood 7 to 10 days before transplanting. Transplant 35 to 40 day old seedlings of tolerant varieties NIAB IRRI-9, KS-282, KSK-133, PK-386, NIAB-2013, Shaheen Basmati, Al-Khalid, or Niji GSR-6.

Direct Seeded Rice:
Approved varieties except Kissan Basmati are suitable. Avoid saline or weedy fields. Per acre seed rate is 8 to 10 kg for fine and 10 to 12 kg for coarse varieties. Sow coarse 20 May to 7 June, Basmati 7 to 25 June. Drill 1.5 inches deep at 9 inches row spacing. Apply pre-emergence herbicide immediately or next day, post-emergence at 15 to 20 days.

Mechanical Transplanting:
Use 100 to 120 trays per acre with 8 to 10 kg fungicide-treated seed, ready in 25 to 30 days. Transplant in leveled, puddled fields in under 1 inch water at 12 inches row spacing, 6 inches plant spacing, and depth under 2 inches.
aspects.varieties:
Punjab Sowing Dates:
Do not sow rice nursery before May 20.
Coarse varieties sow May 20 to June 7 and transplant June 20 to July 7.
Coarse hybrids sow May 20 to June 15 and transplant June 15 to July 15.
Al-Khalid Rice sows May 25 to June 10 and transplants June 20 to July 10.
Basmati varieties sow June 7 to June 25 and transplant July 7 to July 25.
Basmati hybrid KSK-111 sows June 7 to June 25 and transplants July 2 to July 25.
Shaheen Basmati sows June 15 to June 30 and transplants July 15 to July 31.
Special fine varieties Naiji GSR-6, GSR-7, GSR-8, and SKC-BP-32-5-370 sow June 10 to June 25 and transplant July 10 to July 25.
Direct seeding runs May 20 to June 7 for coarse and June 7 to June 25 for Basmati.

Seed Rates and Methods:
Acre seed rate is 4 to 5 kg for Basmati, 6 to 7 kg for coarse, 5 to 6 kg for coarse hybrid, and 8 to 12 kg for direct seeding.
Direct seeding suits all approved varieties except Kissan Basmati.
Per marla dry nursery rate is 1.5 kg for coarse and 750 to 1000 grams for Basmati.
Rab method uses 2 kg coarse and 1 to 1.5 kg Basmati per marla.
Kaddu method uses 1 kg coarse and 500 to 750 grams Basmati per marla.
Machine planting needs 100 to 120 trays and 8 to 10 kg seed per acre.

Seed Treatment and Testing:
Separate light seeds using 25 grams salt per liter water.
Soak seed 24 hours in fungicide with 1.25 times water, then heap in 15 to 20 kg lots for 36 to 48 hours.
Maintain germination above 80 percent tested on 400 seeds.

Field and Fertilizer Management:
Plant 160,000 seedlings per acre at 9 inch spacing with 2 plants per hill.
Average soils require 1.75 bags DAP, 2.5 bags urea, and 1 bag SOP for coarse, and 1.5 bags DAP, 1.75 bags urea, and 1 bag SOP for Basmati.
Coarse hybrid needs 81 kg nitrogen, 46 kg phosphorus, and 25 kg potassium.
Fine hybrid needs 69 kg nitrogen, 40 kg phosphorus, and 25 kg potassium.
Al-Khalid Rice takes maximum 1 bag urea and suits only steam and sella.
Destroy crop stubble by February 28.
Store paddy at 12 to 13 percent moisture.
Sow 15 to 20 kg Jantar seed per acre for green manure.

Varieties and Tolerances:
Coarse yields are 90 to 110 maunds per acre.
Basmati yields are 60 to 77 maunds per acre, while KSK-111 hybrid yields 115 maunds.
NIAB IRRI-9, KS-282, KSK-133, PK-386, NIAB-2013, Shaheen Basmati, Al-Khalid Rice, and Naiji GSR-6 tolerate salinity.
Shaheen Basmati, Super Basmati, KS-282, IRRI-6, KSK-133, and NIAB IRRI-9 resist blast and bakanae.
Super Fine, Supra, Supri, 1847, 7, 1692, 1718, 1885, and 1530 are prohibited.

Punjab Schedule and Stock:
Punjab Seed Corporation holds 81,567 twenty-kilogram bags, including 60,480 Basmati and 21,087 coarse bags.
Kharif 2025 plan issues in April second week, seed delivers May to June, and treatment campaigns run April to October.
aspects.weeds:
Government Incentives:
Registered rice farmers receive certified seed, herbicides, and zinc sulphate at subsidized rates.

Nursery Weed Management:
For pre-emergence weed control, broadcast herbicide using a shaker bottle after puddling, keep water standing for 48 to 72 hours, drain and replace with fresh water two to three times, then broadcast sprouted seed.
For post-emergence control, spray recommended herbicide in tar-wattar condition without standing water.
In loam soils with dry nursery preparation, double plough and plank, broadcast dry seed, and cover with a 1-inch layer of farmyard manure, chaff, rice husk, or straw.
Apply light irrigation by placing dry grass at the inlet, remove straw after a few days, and spray herbicide 15 days after emergence.
Nursery matures in 35 to 40 days.

Cultural and Mechanical Control:
Do not puddle in salt-affected soils.
In non-traditional loam areas, double plough and plank three to four times, apply wattar irrigation to sprout weeds, and cultivate to destroy them before puddling.
Rotate rice with fodder or green manure crops.
Keep 1 to 2 inches of water standing for 20 to 25 days after transplanting.
Clear weeds, especially Dab and Barh grass, from bunds and irrigation channels.
Never hoe immediately after spraying herbicides.

Direct Seeded Rice Weed Management:
Perform double rauni and plough in the first fortnight of May.
Apply pre-emergence herbicide immediately after sowing in wattar, or the next day after irrigation in dry sowing.
Spray post-emergence herbicide 15 to 20 days after sowing in wattar condition, repeat after 40 days if needed, and irrigate 24 to 36 hours later.

Transplanted Rice Pre-emergence Herbicides:
Apply within 1 to 5 days of transplanting and maintain standing water for 4 to 5 days.
Butachlor 60% EC at 800 ml per acre for grasses, sedges, and broadleaves has a pre-harvest interval of 60 days.
Pretilachlor 50% EC at 400 ml per acre has a pre-harvest interval of 60 days.
Bensulfuron plus Acetochlor 14% WP at 350 g per acre has a pre-harvest interval of 21 days.
Butachlor plus Penoxsulam 410 SC at 800 ml per acre has a pre-harvest interval of 60 days.

Direct Seeded Rice Pre-emergence Herbicides:
Triafamone plus Ethoxysulfuron 30% WG at 75 g per acre applied 1 to 3 days after sowing in wattar has a pre-harvest interval of 21 days.
Pendimethalin 33% EC at 1 liter per acre applied 24 to 36 hours after sowing without standing water has a pre-harvest interval of 14 days.

Post-emergence Herbicides:
Spray in tar-wattar within one month of transplanting and irrigate 24 hours later.
Menamifop 10 EC at 500 ml plus Nea Niser at 800 ml per acre controls Ghora grass at the 3 to 4 leaf stage, 12 to 15 days after sowing; irrigate 1 day later, hold water for 5 days; pre-harvest interval is 90 days.
Bispyribac sodium plus Bensulfuron 30% WG or Dibowet at 100 g or 160 ml per acre applied 18 to 22 days after sowing has a pre-harvest interval of 80 days.
Cyhalofop-butyl plus Bispyribac sodium 16% OD at 400 to 500 ml per acre is applied 7 to 14 days after sowing at 3 to 4 leaves.
Penoxsulam plus Fenoxaprop-p-ethyl 10% OD at 250 to 300 ml per acre applied 15 to 21 days after has a pre-harvest interval of 60 days.
Ethoxysulfuron 60% WG at 20 g per acre for Ghoin, Bhoin, Deela, Kutta Kahi, Mirch Booti, and Cho Patti applied 15 to 20 days after has a pre-harvest interval of 21 days.
Cyhalofop-butyl plus Bispyribac sodium plus Penoxsulam 14% OD at 400 to 500 ml per acre applied at 3 to 4 leaves has a pre-harvest interval of 60 days.
Cyhalofop-butyl plus Florpyrauxifen 172 EC at 828 ml per acre applied at 3 to 6 leaves has a pre-harvest interval of 60 days.
Menamifop plus Cyhalofop-butyl 20% EC at 300 ml per acre has a pre-harvest interval of 45 days.

Application Rules:
Use a T-jet nozzle for herbicide application and a hollow-cone nozzle for insecticides.
Spray in the morning after dew dries or in the evening, avoiding strong winds.
